storyboard.claim: The soldiers are slaughtered because the crown is absent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A war icon over a commander slumped in grief at a battlefield loss.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the crown-vacuum setup: the armies are sent out without Diem.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the slaughter to the missing crown, not to enemy strength.
storyboard.staging: Luther slumps under the war icon: the failure is the loss, drawn as a defeat.

storyboard.claim: The host takes Diem's side against the citizens and soldiers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon standing for the defence of Diem.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivot from the defeat to a defence of the absent queen.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the next beats as a defence, not a verdict.
storyboard.staging: No character is shown: the shield and the callout carry the defence.

storyboard.claim: Diem was not on a holiday; she was trapped on a magical island.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The coast of Arboros at the edge of the sea, where Diem is held.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the defence of Diem.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the vacation reading the citizens assume.
storyboard.staging: Shore scene with the rejected phrase struck through: the vacation idea is the wrong reading.

storyboard.claim: Diem was fighting an ancient god to save the whole realm.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The wide Lumnos horizon under a sky, the stage of the god fight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains what Diem was doing on the island.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the enemy: an ancient god, which the citizens did not know.
storyboard.staging: Wide horizon with the callout: the fight happens far from the city, unseen.

storyboard.claim: Does Diem's macro reasoning matter to a mother holding a dead child?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Lumnos horizon, now only ash and ruin.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the defence with the human cost.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the grief in the ruined city, the cost of the macro war.
storyboard.staging: Ruined horizon with the callout: the cost is the ashes, not the strategy.

storyboard.claim: Ilana Hanover uses the public's ignorance as a weapon against Diem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer icon: one person controlling others from behind the scenes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The citizens' ignorance from the previous beat becomes a tool.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Ilana as the one pulling strings, not a neutral critic.
storyboard.staging: Puppeteer icon over the stage: the manipulation is Ilana's, drawn as control.

storyboard.claim: Ilana taunts that the queen was lounging and eating berry tarts while people suffered.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A plate of berry tarts, the literal taunt.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The weapon from the previous beat, in Ilana's own words.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tarts are the taunt itself, a literal claim the crowd is asked to believe.
storyboard.staging: A dessert plate for the taunt: the literal accusation Ilana makes in public.

storyboard.claim: In politics, how things look matters more than the truth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for a political principle; no literal icon fits.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the taunt works.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the political rule that makes the public gap dangerous.
storyboard.staging: Callout alone on the stage: the principle is the words, no icon reads it literally.

storyboard.claim: A crown must show up in person; citizens do not care about the magic behind the absence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The wide Lumnos horizon, the people's view of their absent queen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the perception point to the bond between crown and people.
storyboard.addedInformation: Separates the citizens' view from the magical explanation.
storyboard.staging: Horizon with the callout: the magic is the wrong question for the people.

storyboard.claim: When the dragons came, the queen was not there.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Lumnos horizon, the empty place where the queen should have stood.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the trigger for the citizens' anger.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the moment the absence became visible.
storyboard.staging: Horizon with the callout: the absence at the moment of attack.

storyboard.claim: The grand theoretical bond between crown and people is collapsing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A chains icon: the bond that binds two people, drawn as a failing link.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the realisation that the bond is breaking.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read as the bond itself, the forced tie of the crown.
storyboard.staging: Chains over an abstract field: the bond is the thing failing.

storyboard.claim: Diem's time, energy and presence were consumed by her private bond to Luther.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A heart icon: the mate bond that takes her attention.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the bond is failing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the private mate bond as the consumer of her public duty.
storyboard.staging: Heart icon: the romantic bond draws her energy away from the crown.

storyboard.claim: Her private bond is starving her public duty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-label flow: the private bond feeds into a starved public.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the previous beat into a cause and effect.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the cause-effect explicit as a flow.
storyboard.staging: Flow diagram: the private bond is the cause, the starved public is the effect.

storyboard.claim: With public duty failing and the elite houses turning, who supports Diem?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for the search for allies; no literal icon fits.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows from the failed public duty to the need for allies.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the open question that leads into the council scene.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the question of who backs her is the words, not a picture.

storyboard.claim: The council room is where the elites panic over Diem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The council stage, the room where the arguing happens.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the council scene promised by the question.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the place of the scene for the first time.
storyboard.staging: Stage with the callout: the room is the location of the tension.

storyboard.claim: Luther enters the council room and the room goes quiet.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door icon with Luther walking through it, the threat in his face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The council scene begins with his arrival.
storyboard.addedInformation: The doorway literal: he enters the room as a threat, not a guest.
storyboard.staging: Luther walks through the door with an angry face: the room goes quiet because of him.

storyboard.claim: Luther touches the sigil over his heart and locks eyes on Diem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A heart icon with Luther, hand over the sigil, eyes fixed on the queen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues Luther's entrance into a direct challenge.
storyboard.addedInformation: The heart icon marks the sigil's place on his chest, his loyalty.
storyboard.staging: Luther stands angry with a hand at his heart: a defiant stance toward Diem.

storyboard.claim: In front of the pure-blooded elite, Luther publicly reveals his half-mortal identity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther speaking to the council, a defiant declaration.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The challenge becomes a public declaration.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the declaration as confrontation with the elite.
storyboard.staging: Luther talks angrily at the council: a confrontation, not a comfort.

storyboard.claim: Half mortals are the outcasts of Emarion, shunned by both sides.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An abstract field: the outcast group has no single face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why Luther's declaration matters.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the social status of the group in one phrase.
storyboard.staging: Abstract field with the callout: the group is the subject, not a person.

storyboard.claim: The descended see half mortals as impure abominations, while the mortals see them as oppressors.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An abstract field; both views are carried by the words.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes how each side views the outcasts.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the descended view in the strongest words the narrator uses.
storyboard.staging: Callout alone on the abstract field: the words name the view.

storyboard.claim: Luther declares that half mortals step out of hiding into the light, which is unprecedented.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Open sky, the light the outcasts step into.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the meaning of the declaration.
storyboard.addedInformation: Light stands for leaving the shadows where they hid for their lives.
storyboard.staging: Sky with the callout: the light is the moment they leave the shadows.

storyboard.claim: Loyalty is not about pristine pure blood or a historic family name.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting; the rejected idea is struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Redefines loyalty after the declaration.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the blood-purity view of loyalty.
storyboard.staging: Callout struck through: the blood-purity idea is what the narrator rejects.

storyboard.claim: Loyalty is about who you choose to stand with when the world is ending.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Wide horizon at the end of the world, a choice of allies.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the new definition of loyalty.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes loyalty a choice made in crisis.
storyboard.staging: Wide horizon with the callout: loyalty is the choice made when the world ends.

storyboard.claim: The marginalized, ignored in peacetime, are the ones brave enough to step out of the shadows in a crisis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Silhouetted figures in an abstract field, hidden until they step out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises the outcasts' courage.
storyboard.addedInformation: Silhouettes show the hidden group, not one person.
storyboard.staging: Silhouette with the callout: the shadows are the place the group steps out of.

storyboard.claim: Luther's courage starts an immediate ripple effect in the room.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for the ripple of reaction across the council.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the crisis to the reaction it causes.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the consequence of the declaration.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the ripple is the reaction, carried by the words.

storyboard.claim: Remis Corwo steps up when Luther speaks, though he tried to warn him off.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for the council, where Reis rises to speak.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the next actor in the scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the father's reversal from warning to backing.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the reversal is named, the father is not drawn.

storyboard.claim: Reis tells the council their ancestors did not choose the phoenix sigil for the house to cower.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for Reis's public statement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives Reis's words as the turn.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phrase carries the house's pride in its sigil.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the house's pride is in the words, no icon fits the phoenix.

storyboard.claim: Reis publicly commits House Corwis to the war and overrides the cowardly elites guarding their wealth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A war icon over the wide horizon: the house joins the fight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows Reis's stand into the decision.
storyboard.addedInformation: The war icon marks the house's commitment to the fight.
storyboard.staging: War icon over the horizon with the callout: the house is committed to the battle.

storyboard.claim: Luther choosing the dangerous fight saves Diem's political life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for the political rescue.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the commitment is a rescue.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the outcome for Diem's power.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the rescue is the political outcome, carried by the words.

storyboard.claim: Diem was bleeding support, and Luther gives her a dedicated army.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon over the horizon: the army as protection for the queen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the rescue in military terms.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield reads as the army protecting her.
storyboard.staging: Shield icon with the callout: the army is the protection she gets.

storyboard.claim: Luther's backing of a historic house arrives precisely when Diem is most vulnerable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for the timing of the alliance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Frames the rescue as a well-timed move.
storyboard.addedInformation: Calls it a master stroke, the narrator's praise.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the praise is in the words, no icon for timing.

callout.text: A massive target on her back

storyboard.claim: The alliance may put a massive immediate target on Diem's back instead of saving her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target icon: the queen as the aim of attack.
storyboard.onScreenText: A massive target on her back
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the praise into a doubt.
storyboard.addedInformation: The target icon reads as being aimed at, the danger the narrator raises.
storyboard.staging: Target icon with the callout: the alliance makes her the aim.

storyboard.claim: Penol notes Luther's magic unfurls, shimmering in anticipation of an attack.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther with magic shimmering around him, ready for a fight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows Luther's readiness after the doubt.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shimmer shows the attack is anticipated, not yet begun.
storyboard.staging: Luther stands angry with magic shimmering around him: he is ready to fight.

storyboard.claim: Luther is daring the ruling elite to attack their own queen and is not calming the room.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther pointing at the elite, a confrontation drawn as an accusation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows from his readiness to a direct challenge.
storyboard.addedInformation: The point reads as a dare, not a plea.
storyboard.staging: Luther points angrily at the elite: the dare is his act, not a calming gesture.

callout.text: A lit match in a powder keg

storyboard.claim: Luther is holding a detonator, escalating tension to the brink of violence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther speaking angrily at the council, the danger in his voice.
storyboard.onScreenText: A lit match in a powder keg
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Escalates the dare into the brink of violence.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout is the metaphor the narrator uses, carried in words, not an icon.
storyboard.staging: Luther talks angrily: the escalation is the threat in his face and words.

storyboard.claim: Luther has no other choice because his inescapable magical bond to Diem forces him to drag his people out.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains icon with Luther thinking, bound by the forced bond.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the reason for the escalation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read as the bond that binds him against his will.
storyboard.staging: Luther thinks with a worried face under chains: a bond he cannot escape.

storyboard.claim: Luther ties the survival of all half mortals to Diem's reign.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for the wager he makes for his people.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the stake of the bond.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the wager in plain words.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the wager is the words, the stake is the reign.

storyboard.claim: Luther says if she falls we all burn, forcing a bond neither side asked for.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Abstract field; the forced bond is carried by the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the Luther speech with the forced bond.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the forced bond the claim, with no literal icon for burning.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the abstract field: the forced bond is what the narrator names.

storyboard.claim: Dictating a continent's fate traces back to the original sins of this world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for the temple on Corel, where the history is revealed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the scene back to the island of Corel.
storyboard.addedInformation: Links the bond to the world's first crime.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the return to Corel is the words, the temple is the place.

storyboard.claim: The revealed history recontextualizes the entire war.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for the Corel revelation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the atmosphere of the Corel revelation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the revelation changes the meaning of the whole war.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the revelation changes the war, carried by the words.
